sections.h2: Where is Christian County, Missouri, and who bills its property tax?
sections.html:
Christian County sits in the Ozarks of southwest Missouri, between Springfield and Branson. Ozark is the county seat and Nixa is the largest city. The county covers 564 square miles, and neighbors include Greene County to the north, Webster and Douglas to the east, Taney to the south and Stone and Lawrence to the west. Part of the Mark Twain National Forest lies inside its borders, and the James River and branches of the White River drain it.

Growth has been steady. The county's own site notes that the 1980 population of 22,402 rose by nearly 150 percent to 54,285 by 2000. The 2020 census counted 88,842 people, and the Census Bureau's July 2025 estimate is 96,725. Property tax is billed by the Collector of Revenue and valued by the Assessor, both in the historic courthouse on the square in Ozark.

sections.h2: How do I reach the Christian County Collector and Assessor?
sections.html:
• Collector of Revenue: Ted Nichols, 100 W. Church, Room 101, Ozark, MO 65721, (417) 582-4330, open Monday through Friday from 8:00 a.m. to 4:30 p.m. including the lunch hour.
  • Assessor: Jeremy Burns. Real estate questions go to 417-582-4310 and personal property to 417-582-4320.
  • Payments: in person, by mail, online at christiancountycollector.com, by the toll-free number printed on the bill, or in the 24-hour drop box on the west side of the courthouse.

The Collector's page says the office collects what the Assessor's records show and cannot change a statement on its own. Errors in a mailing address, vehicle list or legal description go to the Assessor before payment. Partial payments and wrong amounts are not accepted.

sections.h2: When are 2026 Christian County property taxes due?
sections.html:
Statements for 2026 were scheduled to be mailed on November 2, 2026. They are due on receipt and become delinquent after December 31. A mailed payment must carry a USPS postmark of 12/31/26, and the online payment page closes at 11:59 p.m. that night. The Collector warns that technical trouble with phone or web payment does not extend the deadline.

Residents of four smaller towns get an in-person option. For one day each, from 9 a.m. to noon, the Collector's staff will take payments at city halls: Billings on November 16, Clever on November 17, Sparta on November 18 and Highlandville on November 19, 2026. Bring the whole statement. Those stops accept cash, check or money order only, and checks must be in blue or black ink.

If no statement arrives by the end of November, call the office. Failing to receive a bill does not remove the duty to pay.

sections.h2: What does it cost to pay Christian County tax electronically?
sections.html:
Electronic payment fees are not part of the tax. The Collector's page says the county receives none of the service fee and points to RSMo 139.055, which lets the cost fall only on those who choose to pay electronically.

Way to payFeeSource
E-check$2.00Christian County Collector
Debit card$4.00Christian County Collector
Credit card2.45 percent of the balanceChristian County Collector
Cash, personal check, cashier's check or money order at the office or drop boxNo service fee listedChristian County Collector

The Collector adds that a paid receipt can be shown from a phone screen at the DMV or Department of Revenue.

sections.h2: How does the Christian County Assessor value property?
sections.html:
The Assessor's office values everything taxable in the county as of January 1. Its page lists more than 42,951 real estate parcels and over 38,457 personal property accounts, with a total assessed value above $2 billion for 2025. Assessed value is a share of market value that depends on class: 19 percent for residential, 32 percent for commercial and 12 percent for agricultural land.

Value is one half of the bill. The other half is the levy set by each taxing district. The Assessor counts thirteen school districts, eight road districts, ten cities, nine fire districts and nine other levy districts, such as ambulance, senior services and the junior college. Totals therefore differ from one part of the county to another, and the district names on a bill explain why. Value Change Notices, exemption applications and address change forms are on the Assessor's page.

sections.h2: How do I appeal a Christian County assessment?
sections.html:
Missouri gives every owner a path from the Assessor to a county board and then to the State Tax Commission. Under RSMo 137.275, a Board of Equalization appeal must be lodged on or before the second Monday in July. A later appeal to the commission under RSMo 138.430 is due within the chapter 138 deadline or 30 days after the board's final action, whichever is later.

  • Look at the Value Change Notice and the market data on the Assessor's page.
  • Call the real estate line at 417-582-4310 to ask for an informal review.
  • Ask the County Clerk for the board's form and hearing dates.
  • If a property's assessed value rose 15 percent or more, RSMo 138.060 puts the burden of proof on the Assessor, apart from increases caused by new construction.

sections.h2: Who qualifies for the Christian County senior tax credit?
sections.html:
The Senate Bill 190 senior citizen real estate tax credit has strict rules, posted on both the county home page and the Assessor's page. Renewal for people already approved is automatic if they still qualify and made no new improvements, though a spouse who has newly reached the age needs an application.

  • First-time applications are available March 1, 2027 and accepted until June 15, 2027 at the Collector's office, Room 101.
  • The applicant must be at least 62 by midnight December 31, 2026.
  • The home must be in Christian County and the applicant's primary residence since at least June 29, 2026.
  • 2026 taxes must be paid, the personal property assessment must be completed and every applicant signature must be notarized.

sections.h2: What should a Christian County seller do about the tax bill?
sections.html:
The Collector's page states that the current owner is responsible for all taxes due on the property, and that tax obligation is fixed as of January 1. Ask the title company how the closing statement divides the year, and ask the Collector for the exact balance before the closing date.

Census Bureau QuickFacts for the county show a median owner-occupied home value of $274,900 for 2020 to 2024, a median household income of $83,437 and 75.9 percent owner occupancy. The county had 38,594 housing units in 2025 and issued 495 building permits that year. The average commute is 25.5 minutes, and 89.6 percent of residents lived in the same house a year earlier.

faqs.q: What is the deadline to pay Christian County, MO property taxes for 2026?
faqs.a: December 31, 2026. A mailed payment needs a USPS postmark of 12/31/26, and the online system closes at 11:59 p.m. that night. Taxes become delinquent after that date, and the Collector says phone or web trouble does not extend the deadline.

faqs.q: Where do I pay Christian County property taxes in person?
faqs.a: At the Collector's office, 100 W. Church, Room 101, in Ozark, Monday through Friday from 8:00 a.m. to 4:30 p.m. There is also a 24-hour drop box on the west side of the courthouse. Courtesy payment days are set for Billings, Clever, Sparta and Highlandville on November 16 through 19, 2026.

faqs.q: What does it cost to pay Christian County tax by card?
faqs.a: Credit cards add 2.45 percent of the balance, debit cards add $4.00 and e-checks add $2.00. The county does not receive that service fee. Payments made in person with cash, check or money order carry no listed fee.

faqs.q: Who sets the value of my Christian County home?
faqs.a: The Christian County Assessor, Jeremy Burns, values property as of January 1 and applies the state rates of 19 percent for residential, 32 percent for commercial and 12 percent for agricultural land. Call 417-582-4310 about real estate. Tax districts then apply their own levies to that assessed value.

faqs.q: Can seniors reduce their Christian County tax bill?
faqs.a: Possibly, through the SB 190 senior citizen real estate tax credit. First-time applications open March 1, 2027 and close June 15, 2027, and the applicant must have turned 62 by December 31, 2026. Approved owners renew automatically. Applications go to the Collector's office in Ozark.
